newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-INDIANS GIVE TWO-YEAR EXTENSION TO MANAGER HARGROVE.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-INDIANS GIVE TWO-YEAR EXTENSION TO MANAGER HARGROVE.

text.p: Mike Hargrove, who has guided the Cleveland Indians to back-to-back division titles and the team's first World Series appearance in over four decades, agreed to a two-year contract extension Tuesday.
The 47-year-old Hargrove was in the sixth and final year of a contract. The club holds an option for the 2000 season.
"Mike Hargrove has done everything asked of him for this organisation as player, coach and manager over the past 19 years," said Indians executive vice president and general manager John Hart.
"He has been at the core of our success over the last four seasons and we look forward to him guiding the club into the next century."
The Indians are just 17-18 and enter Tuesday night's game at Texas in third place in the American League Central. Hargrove has a 466-396 record since taking over the Tribe in 1991.

The Indians won 100 games in 1995 and advanced to their first World Series since 1954, but lost to the Atlanta Braves in six games. Cleveland was 99-62 under Hargrove last season before losing to the Baltimore Orioles in the Division Series.
